title: Helping a neighbour you barely know

body.heading: Start with the low doors
paragraphs: Neighbourly help begins at ankle height: the bin brought in, the parcel taken in, the ladder lent without a form in triplicate. These small exchanges are how streets quietly audit each other and decide who can be trusted with the bigger things.
You do not need to know their story to start. You need only to be visibly, mildly useful over time.

body.heading: Make help easy to repay — or not
paragraphs: The genius of neighbour-help is its loose accounting. The ladder comes back with biscuits; the parcel favour returns as a watched house during holidays. Keep the ledger deliberately fuzzy. Precise accounting between neighbours converts a community into a market, and markets are colder.
If someone insists on repaying formally, accept graciously. Refusing all repayment can be its own kind of pride.

body.heading: Be there before the emergency
paragraphs: The time to learn a neighbour’s name is not during the flood, the blackout, or the ambulance visit — though those moments will come, and streets that know themselves cope with them entirely differently from streets that do not.
A name, a wave, one small favour banked: that is the whole infrastructure. Build it in peacetime.

takeaway: Start with bins and ladders, keep the accounting fuzzy, and learn names before you need them.
